items.content:
The Ware for October 2026 is shown below:

Another contribution from FETguy and Renew Computers! I found this board to be interesting mainly because I always wondered how these things . The construction reveals a trick which ended up as a surprise, at least to me!

A couple of administrative notes – I am counting my blessings that this site is still up despite the heightened level of CVE’s. This is an aging WordPress blog (its origins pre-date “the cloud” and HTML5!), which uses PHP at its core, and kudos to Pair Networks for being on top of it and keeping this bit of infrastructure up and running. That being said, I don’t think we’re out of the thick of it so I fully expect some downtime in the near future.

Also, if you’re wondering what I’m up to on Baochip, I do weekly updates on Discord in Baochip’s #the-commit-log channel. I only cross-post long-read technimaterials and the monthly name that ware to the blog, keeping in line with my historical practices here.

items.title: Winner, Name that Ware September 2026
items.author: bunnie
items.content:
The Ware for September 2026 is a tire pressure monitor from a late 80’s to early 90’s model Porsche, made by Bosch. According to the submitter:

Apparently they were deeply unpopular since the sensor mechanism used transponders fitted into pockets in special wheels, which meant lots of alarms when owners changed to wheels without the transponders. Each wheel’s suspension mounted an antenna operating at a “high frequency” of probably a few MHz. When a tire’s pressure dropped below a threshold, a pressure switch in the transponder would open or close, which would change the signal sent back, and this unit would notice and signal the instrument cluster.

Kind of a crazy piece of hardware for the late 80’s – this would be pretty cutting edge for the time. Nobody quite got what the part was – but Drew Macrae noticed the Bosch logo peeking between the pins, which caused me to take a second look at the photo. Good eye, I missed that on my redaction. I’ll give the prize to Drew for calling that one out. I really had to search for it, even when told where it was. Congrats, email me for your prize!
